VaultDB Core — Developer Documentation

VaultDB Core is the foundational infrastructure layer of the KRONOS Re platform. It provides data orchestration, task execution, authentication, and API services that all domain modules build upon.

Key Capabilities

Data Layer — DuckLake ORM

VaultDB uses DuckLake (DuckDB-backed, Parquet on S3) for persistent storage with an ORM-like interface:

  • Model classes map Python objects to DuckLake tables with typed columns
  • Virtual Forks provide isolated sandbox schemas (sandbox_<role>) that overlay production data via SQL pushdown
  • Inherited reads merge sandbox overrides with production data transparently
  • Time-series models support point-in-time historical queries on DuckLake versions

Task Execution Dispatcher (TED)

TED provides a unified task interface that routes computation to the appropriate backend:

Runner Backend Use Case
LOCAL In-process Development and testing
SERVICE Celery + Redis Async background jobs
BATCH AWS Batch (Fargate) Long-running computations, GPU workloads
FUNCTION AWS Lambda Event-driven, short-lived tasks 
from vaultdb._state import TED

@TED.task()
def compute_reserves(block_id: str, basis: str) -> dict:
    # Runs on whichever backend is configured
    ...

# Submit asynchronously
result = compute_reserves.apply_async(kwargs={"block_id": "TED-FA-2026", "basis": "STAT"})
status = result.status   # SUBMITTED, STARTED, SUCCESS, FAILURE
value = result.get(timeout=60)

Workflow Engine

The workflow engine manages multi-step computational pipelines:

  1. AI proposes a workflow as a JSON definition (steps with dependencies)
  2. Human reviews the workflow DAG in the dashboard
  3. Human approves with a cryptographically signed approval record
  4. Engine executes steps in topological order, resolving inter-step references
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> PENDING_APPROVAL: Workflow proposed
    PENDING_APPROVAL --> APPROVED: Human approval
    PENDING_APPROVAL --> REJECTED: Human rejection
    APPROVED --> RUNNING: Execution started
    RUNNING --> DONE: All steps complete
    RUNNING --> FAILED: Step failure

Approval Engine

Every material action requires a cryptographically verified human approval:

  • HMAC-SHA256 tokens bind approvals to specific subjects and approver identities
  • Versioned keys support seamless key rotation
  • Policy rules enforce separation of duties, role requirements, review time minimums
  • Immutable audit trail captures full OIDC claims, IP address, and review notes

Authentication

Multi-provider authentication with role-based access control:

  • OIDC: AWS Cognito, Azure Entra ID, Auth0, Okta
  • GitHub: OAuth2 with opaque token support
  • AWS Bridge: OIDC tokens exchange for AWS credentials via Cognito Identity Pools
  • RBAC: Role extraction from JWT claims (groups, roles, Keycloak realm_access)

Web API

FastAPI application with:

  • OAuth2/OIDC login flow
  • Task submission and status polling endpoints
  • Scheduled task management
  • Bearer token and session cookie authentication

Getting Started

Installation

pip install vaultdb.core

Configuration

All configuration flows through vaultdb.config:

from vaultdb import config

# Configuration is loaded from:
# 1. ./vaultdb_config.py (project-local)
# 2. ~/.vaultdb/vaultdb_config.py (user-global)
# 3. Environment variables (highest priority)

Running the API Server

# Development mode
export DEBUG=true
python -m vaultdb.web  # http://localhost:8000

# Production
uvicorn vaultdb.web:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Architecture Standards

  • Python 3.12+ with strict typing (disallow_untyped_defs = True)
  • Ruff for formatting and linting (160 char line limit)
  • MyPy for static type checking
  • Pytest with >90% coverage target
  • Vectorization first — Arrow/DuckDB compute over Python loops
